message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-11-14 13:10 IST to 2026-11-15 13:10 IST (2026-11-14 07:40 UTC to 2026-11-15 07:40 UTC)  
**Scope:** DLL_software_component.txt only. Obvious naming variants were normalized and duplicate component families were merged. Products.txt and List_of_SIA_Completed.txt were not read or combined.

No credible vulnerability newly reported, materially updated, or newly surfaced within the exact 24-hour window could be tied confidently to a component in the assigned DLL inventory.

### MongoDB ecosystem coverage

The mandatory dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, major maintained libraries and services, MongoDB-owned alerts, CVE/NVD records, GitHub Security Advisories, CISA sources, and credible security research.

No MongoDB finding fell inside the scan window. MongoDB's authoritative alert feed showed its newest security bulletins on November 10, before this run's cutoff.

### Validation notes

- Recent Telerik and Kendo advisories that could resemble inventory matches were published November 11-13 and were excluded as stale.
- GitHub's November 14 advisory feed and contemporaneous CVE reporting were checked; the new records found concerned unrelated products and did not match the DLL inventory.
- No new CISA KEV addition in the window mapped to the assigned components.
- No uncertain product-family match remained credible enough for a "Possible matches needing review" section.

Sources checked included [MongoDB security alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts), the [GitHub Advisory Database for November 14](https://github.com/advisories?query=published%3A2026-11-14), the [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security Progress advisory](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/progress-software-security-advisory-av26-1148), and the [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

**Closing:** No immediate review is recommended based solely on new disclosures in this scan window. Previously reported vulnerabilities and normal patch obligations remain outside this last-24-hours digest.
